content: The ear canal, also referred to as the external auditory meatus or external acoustic meatus, is a tubular structure that connects the outer ear to the middle ear. In humans, the ear canal extends from the pinna (the external part of the ear) to the eardrum. It measures approximately 26 millimeters in length and 7 millimeters in diameter. The dimensions and shape of the ear canal can vary significantly between individuals. This variability is an important consideration when fitting hearing protection devices, as the size and shape of the canal can influence the effectiveness of such devices. Due to its exposure to the external environment, the ear canal is particularly susceptible to various diseases and disorders. Common conditions affecting the ear canal include: Otitis externa (swimmer's ear): This is an inflammation of the ear canal caused by bacterial infection. Contact dermatitis: An allergic or irritant reaction affecting the skin of the ear canal. Ear fungus: A fungal infection of the ear canal. Ear myiasis: A rare condition involving the infestation of the ear canal by maggots. Bone exposure: This occurs when the skin within the ear canal wears away, exposing the underlying bone. Granuloma: A type of scar tissue, often resulting from the use of tympanostomy tubes. Stenosis: A gradual narrowing of the ear canal. Foreign bodies in the ear: Objects lodged in the ear canal. Ear mites: Commonly seen in animals, these parasites can infest the ear canal. Cysts of the external auditory meatus: These include epidermal cysts, which can vary in size and may require medical attention. Earwax, also known as cerumen, is a yellowish, waxy substance secreted within the ear canal. It serves several important functions, including cleaning and lubricating the ear canal. Additionally, earwax provides a protective barrier against bacteria, fungi, and insects. However, excessive or impacted cerumen can lead to complications. It may press against the eardrum or block the external auditory canal, potentially impairing hearing.
